title: 5.6.3 Lab: A chime on every bumper hit
description: The three-bumper table from 5.4.5 scores, but it is silent. Load a chime once, in setup(), and play it in the one place a hit happens exactly once, so each drop gives three chimes and never a buzz. Most browsers keep a page silent until you click it or press a key, so if the first drop is quiet, click the game and press R.
unit: 5.6 Pinball: a sound on a hit

steps.title: Load the chime in setup()
steps.instructions:
Run the starter first. It is the three-bumper table from 5.4.5: the ball rolls down bumpers worth 1, 5 and 10, and one drop scores 16. It makes no sound: sound is this lab.

`loadSound(name)` starts downloading one of the course's sounds and hands you back a sound straight away. Keep it in a variable, the way you keep a sprite: the starter already has `let chime;` at the top. The course's short chime is called `'coin'`. Type the name exactly, quotes included: a misspelled name never plays, and the console says why.

Load it once, in `setup()`. The file takes a moment to arrive, and `draw()` runs 60 times a second, so a `loadSound` there would start a new download every frame and none would ever be ready. In `setup()`, where the STEP 1 comment is, add:

```js
chime = loadSound('coin');
```

Write it with no `let` in front, the way `player = new Sprite(...)` is written in 5.1.8. The `let chime;` at the top already made the variable; a `let` inside `setup()` would make a second `chime` that only `setup()` can see, and `draw()` would stop with an error at the first hit.
hints: Check the name letter by letter: coin, all lower case, inside quotes.
It goes inside setup()'s braces, after score = 0;, not at the top of the file and not in draw().

steps.title: Play it once for each hit
steps.instructions:
`chime.play();` plays the chime once, from the start. Each call starts a fresh copy, so it has to go in the one place where a hit happens **exactly once**: inside the `if (touching && !b.wasTouching) { ... }` block in `draw()`, next to `score += b.worth;`, where the STEP 2 comment is. That `if` is true only on the frame a touch starts (5.4.1), which is why the score goes up once per hit. The chime goes in the same place, so it plays once per hit too.

Not under `if (touching)` or `if (ball.colliding(b))` alone: those are true on every frame the ball touches, so the chime would start about 60 times a second, a buzz instead of a ding. Not straight in `draw()` either: that buzzes all the time.
hints: The new line goes between the { and } of if (touching && !b.wasTouching), above or below score += b.worth;.
One line is enough: the loop runs that if for every bumper, so all three bumpers chime.

steps.title: Click, drop, listen
steps.instructions:
Run it. Most browsers will not let a web page make a sound until the person using it has clicked on it or pressed a key on it, so the page knows someone is there. moSHion switches sound on the first time you click the game or press a key in it; you write nothing for that. Whether your click on Run already counts depends on the browser.

So if the first drop is silent, click the game, then press R to drop the ball again. You should hear three chimes per drop, one for each bumper, as the score goes 1, then 6, then 16. Still nothing? Check the name letter by letter and look in the console, then check that the browser tab and your speakers are not muted.

Too loud? A sound's `.volume` runs from 0 (silent) to 1 (full, where every sound starts). Try `chime.volume = 0.5;` in `setup()`, on the line after the `loadSound`.
hints: Three chimes for one drop means each hit plays once. A long buzz means .play() is somewhere that runs on every frame of a touch.

requirements.title: The chime is loaded once, in setup()
requirements.description: Inside setup(), a variable you made at the top of the file is set with loadSound('coin') (the full path '/moshion/assets/coin.wav' counts too; any quotes, any variable name), and no loadSound is left in draw(). Help: 5.6.1 (Reading: A sound on a hit)
requirements.hint: In setup(), write chime = loadSound('coin'); with no let in front. Check the name letter by letter ('coin'), and keep loadSound out of draw().

requirements.title: A hit plays the chime once
requirements.description: A sound's .play() runs inside the if that is true only on the frame a touch starts, touching && !b.wasTouching, next to the score, so each bumper hit gives one chime. Help: 5.6.1 (Reading: A sound on a hit)
requirements.hint: Put chime.play(); between the { and } of if (touching && !b.wasTouching), next to score += b.worth;.

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.6.3 Lab: A chime on every bumper hit". The task they were given: The starter is a pinball table with three bumpers in the array bumpers, worth 1, 5 and 10, scored in a loop with an edge check (touching now and not touching last frame, by each bumper's own wasTouching). It is silent. In setup(), load the course's chime by its name, loadSound('coin'), into the variable chime that the starter already declares at the top with let. Then play the chime with its play() method inside the if that adds the bumper's worth, so it plays once per hit. Optionally set the chime's volume. What the starter file already had: walls, the three bumpers with worth and wasTouching, a ground, a ball that rolls, the score and its edge-checked loop in draw(), an R key that drops the ball again, and let chime; declared at the top with nothing loaded into it. The starter meets none of the criteria. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, if / else chains or ternaries, helper functions, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or inside a string never runs, so a line the student only wrote in a comment does not count. moSHion facts that matter here: loadSound(name) starts downloading the built-in sound with that name (loadSound(path) a file) and returns a sound at once; play() before the file has arrived does nothing, so sounds are loaded once in setup(). A loadSound in draw() (or update()) runs every frame and starts a new download each time, so the sound never gets to play. The built-in names include 'coin' (a short chime) and 'music' (a tune); the full path /moshion/assets/coin.wav, and assets/coin.wav or ./assets/coin.wav, reach the same file and count the same. A misspelled name or path never plays (the console prints a warning). A let or const in front of the assignment inside setup() makes a new variable only setup() can see, so draw() would stop with an error at the first hit. play() starts a fresh copy every call. .volume runs from 0 to 1 and is optional here. ball.colliding(b) is 0 while apart and a count of frames while touching, so an if on it alone (or on touching alone) is true on every frame of a touch and would play about 60 chimes a second; the if that adds the worth is true only on the frame a touch starts. A memory test written as === false while the memory holds colliding()'s number is never true; ! and == false both work. A helper function that the hit's if calls counts as playing in that if. A browser makes no sound until the player clicks or presses a key on the game; moSHion handles that by itself, so the student writes nothing for it. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old reader: short sentences and plain, everyday words.

rubric.title: The chime is loaded once, in setup()
rubric.description: Inside setup(), a variable declared at the top of the file is given loadSound(...) with the course's chime, loadSound('coin') ('music', or a full path such as /moshion/assets/coin.wav or assets/coin.wav, also reach a real file). Any quotes and any variable name count, and so does keeping the sound on each bumper or in a list, as long as it is loaded in setup(). Not met: a let or const in front of it inside setup(), a misspelled name or path, the load only in a comment, or any loadSound left in draw(). Help: 5.6.1 (Reading: A sound on a hit)

rubric.title: A hit plays the chime once
rubric.description: A sound's play() runs only on the frame a bumper hit starts: inside the if that tests touching now and not touching last frame (the one that adds the bumper's worth), in an if nested inside it, or in a helper that if calls. Playing it above or below the score line both count. Not met: play() straight in draw() or in the loop outside that if, under an if on colliding() or touching alone, in that if's else, under a key press, or only in setup(). Help: 5.6.1 (Reading: A sound on a hit)
